subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should OpenClaw solve this as a narrow per-job and heartbeat elevated authority marker, or fold the elevated-exec requirement into the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance design?
rationale: The choice defines when autonomous cron and heartbeat turns may inherit host-elevated exec authority and affects persisted cron/API shape, heartbeat config semantics, migration, and compatibility.

options.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
options.body: Treat this issue as the elevated-exec requirement for the broader scheduling provenance design while explicitly keeping heartbeat provenance in scope.

options.title: Implement Narrow Elevated Markers
options.body: Add per-job and heartbeat-modifier elevated approval state now, with tests for create, update, execution, and migration behavior.

options.title: Fail Closed For Internal Sources
options.body: Remove cron-event and heartbeat wildcard elevation as a compatibility-breaking hardening step only if maintainers accept the upgrade impact.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
recommendation.body: Treat this issue as the elevated-exec requirement for the broader scheduling provenance design while explicitly keeping heartbeat provenance in scope.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent agent cron caller-scope work makes this the closest current owner path for scheduling provenance decisions.
